1764 |       SEC.INTRO:
1765 |         text: |
1766 |           *(Soft Rhodes keys, distant organ swells, deep bass humming, and a gentle brushed snare as the choir hums in harmony.)*
1767 |           [Lead:]
1768 |           Ohhh, you gotta get ready now… (mmm-hmm)
1769 |           Ohhh, no man knows the day or the hour…
1770 |       SEC.V1:
1771 |         text: |
1772 |           Get your house in order, oh do it today
1773 |           Get your house in order, oh do it right away
1774 |           For Jesus is coming, no man knows where or when
1775 |           Get your house in order, for He’s coming back again
1776 |       SEC.CH1:
1777 |         text: |
1778 |           **(Lead:)** Get your house in order... *(Choir echoes: In order!)*
1779 |           **(Lead:)** Oh, don’t wait too late... *(Choir echoes: Don’t wait!)*
1780 |           For Jesus is coming... *(Choir: Coming!)*
1781 |           He's coming back again
1782 |           *(Soft instrumental break – bluesy guitar and organ swells as the choir hums in harmony.)*
1783 |       SEC.V2:
1784 |         text: |
1785 |           There’s earthquakes, hurricanes, famines, and disease
1786 |           Can’t you hear the Lord is callin’?
1787 |           You better take heed...
1788 |           So many homeless, lost out in the cold
1789 |           But my God’s got mansions
1790 |           More precious than gold
1791 |       SEC.CH2:
1792 |         text: |
1793 |           Get your house in order, oh do it today
1794 |           Get your house in order, oh do it right away
1795 |           For Jesus is coming, no man knows where or when
1796 |           Get your house in order, for He’s coming back again
1797 |       SEC.BRIDGE:
1798 |         text: |
1799 |           *(The music softens, Rhodes and bass pulsing gently, as the lead starts to testify.)*
1800 |           [Lead:]
1801 |           Ohh, but there’s something, something about His name...
1802 |           *(Choir hums in agreement, warm harmonies swelling.)*
1803 |           *(Rhodes swells, drums build lightly, leading into the next movement…)*
1804 |       SEC.WORSHIP:
1805 |         text: |
1806 |           *(Organ swells, deepening bass, light hi-hats as the choir takes the lead.)*
1807 |           Something about the name Jesus,
1808 |           Something about the name Jesus,
1809 |           It is the sweetest name I know...
1810 |           Oh, how I love the name Jesus,
1811 |           Oh, how I love the name Jesus,
1812 |           It is the sweetest name I know...
1813 |           *(Lead with passion, choir responding powerfully.)*
1814 |           [Lead:] Some say it’s like fire shut up in my bones…
1815 |           [Choir:] Fire in my bones!
1816 |           [Lead:] Oh, the Holy Ghost is moving, I can feel it strong…
1817 |           [Choir:] He won’t leave us alone!
1818 |           Something about the name Jesus,
1819 |           Something about the name Jesus,
1820 |           It is the sweetest name I know…
1821 |       SEC.OUTRO:
1822 |         text: |
1823 |           *(Soft Rhodes, deep bass, and light drum taps as the energy comes back down.)*
1824 |           Get your house in order, oh do it today…
1825 |           Get your house in order, oh don’t delay…
1826 |           *(Lead whispers, choir softly echoing: “For He’s coming… back… again…”)

1963 | 1) SHOW SUMMARY (966 chars)
1964 | Southern gospel blues anthem with Texas barroom grit and Houston pocket. One consistent male lead delivers urgent warning lines and then lifts into praise while a mixed choir answers in tight call and response. Core band is a three sax frontline: fast attack alto for hissy stabs and runs, tenor for body counterlines, and bass sax for low mid authority and riffs. Tribal toms and hand percussion drive a laid back 4 4 groove under Rhodes and Hammond swells with sparse blues guitar turnarounds. Energy curve: humble intro with choir hum, stripped verse preaching, hook hits with choir answers, breakdown testimony, then a full worship peak on Something about the name Jesus and Fire in my bones before a reflective outro. Mix intent is warm live room, vocal forward, mono low end, wide sax spread, no shimmer. Use a brief stop time before the worship entry and let sax answer phrase ends. Choir stays human and restrained in verses and opens wide on the final lift.

2615 | 
2616 | We are building this record together as a Texas rooted gospel blues statement in 6 8 where your lived Southern lineage stays front and center and the Houston pocket lives inside the swing rather than on top of it. The arrangement is intentionally spare and human with one consistent male lead carrying the entire narrative in a close mic preaching sung delivery while the choir functions strictly as supportive adlibs and response energy instead of a second lead. The sonic fingerprint is the three sax frontline with fast attack alto providing sharp stabs and hissy runs tenor supplying body and answering counterlines and bass sax anchoring the low mids so the groove feels heavy without getting cloudy. Tribal toms hand percussion and shakers drive the roll and the Rhodes plus Hammond swells frame the worship atmosphere with sparse blues guitar punctuation. The emotional curve moves from quiet warning to urgent hook to testimony breakdown then a full worship peak on Something about the name Jesus before settling back into a warm reflective outro. Mix intent is live room realism with mono bass dark plate on hooks phone safe midrange and a clean spinback exit with vinyl hiss while avoiding shimmer and keeping the lead intelligible on Jesus and sweetest at all times.

2802 | Thought for 14s
2803 | Co-created Show Summary
2804 | We are co-creating a 6/8th Southern gospel blues record rooted in Texas grit and Southern Baptist truth with a Houston pocket that lives inside the swing. The lead is a small town Black woman contralto with near baritone grit and a smokey bourbon tone shaped by church and sharpened by five years of operatic training with four octave control. The arrangement stays human and intentional with tribal toms hand percussion and shakers rolling the 6/8th feel while Rhodes and Hammond frame the worship air. The signature is a three sax frontline where fast attack alto delivers short hissy stabs and runs tenor carries body answers and bass sax anchors low mids without masking the voice. Energy moves from quiet warning to urgent hook to testimony breakdown exposing whisper and fry then rises into a controlled belt at the worship peak before settling into a warm reflective outro. Mix intent is live room realism with mono bass dark plate on hooks phone safe mids and a clean spinback exit with vinyl hiss while keeping Jesus and sweetest intelligible at all times and preventing shimmer.

3402 | Artist Bio 1997 chars no song data
3403 | Born in a small Southern town and raised in the heat of a Baptist church sanctuary, mo$ is a contralto with near-baritone grit and a smoke-and-bourbon warmth that feels lived in. Her voice moves like a working instrument: grounded in gut-sung testimony, refined by years of operatic discipline, and fearless enough to bend microtones, slide into fry, or drop from a controlled belt to a whispered confession without losing the story.
3404 | 
3405 | As an artist, she treats tradition as a backbone, not a cage. She carries the spiritual urgency of old gospel, the bruised truth of the blues, and the porch-to-juke-joint realism of Southern music culture, while letting modern Southern rhythm and Houston pocket inform the way the music breathes. Her listening map runs from Robert Johnson’s haunted minimalism to Hank Jr.’s hard-edged drawl and the wild Southern swagger of Skynyrd—then flips into funk and jazz discipline for timing, harmony, and touch.
3406 | 
3407 | mo$ is most at home chasing authenticity in bars, juke joints, and late-night jam sessions, learning the room the way a preacher learns a congregation. She writes and performs to make the sacred feel immediate: lived faith, hard days, redemption, and the communal electricity of call-and-response. The production philosophy is simple—human first, artifacts last—capturing breath, edge, and space on purpose, then shaping it with precision. She’s not chasing perfection as polish; she’s chasing precision as truth. That means clear diction when it counts, intentional grit when it matters, and dynamics that move like real breath. In every project, mo$ aims to honor the elders, advance the lineage, and leave enough open space for listeners to hear themselves inside the music. The result is a catalog that feels southern, fearless, and unmistakably hers.
3408 | Co created Show Summary 967 chars
3409 | We co created a 6/8th Southern gospel blues record that feels like Texas grit in a live room with a Houston pocket sitting inside the swing. The lead is a small town Black woman contralto with near baritone grit and smokey bourbon warmth shaped by Southern Baptist church roots and sharpened by operatic training so she can move from chest power to whisper and fry with microtonal control. Tribal toms and hand percussion drive the roll while Rhodes and Hammond swells hold the sanctuary air and sparse blues guitar punctuates the turns. A three sax frontline is the signature with fast attack alto stabs and runs tenor answers for body and bass sax anchoring low mids without masking the lead. The arc moves from warning verses to call and response hooks into a testimony breakdown then a full worship peak on the name Jesus before a warm reflective outro with spinback and vinyl hiss. Mix intent is mono bass with dark plate on hooks phone safe mids and no shimmer.

We cannot understand much about any thing or idea, or system of things or ideas, without understanding the relationships between or among the ideas or systems. There are many important types of relationships: causal, correlation, feedback, inputs/outputs, influence, direct/indirect, etc. At the most fundamental level though, all types of relationships require that we consider two underlying elements: action and reaction, or the mutual effects of two or more things. Gaining an aware- ness of the numerous interrelationships around us forms an ecological ethos that connects us in an infinite network of interactions. Action-reaction relationships are not merely important to understanding physical systems, but are an essential metacognitive trait for understanding human social dynamics and the essential interplay between our thoughts (cognition), feelings (emotion), and motivations (conation). Relationships are a crucial component of the DSRP framework (Distinctions, Systems, Relationships, Perspectives). Key points about Relationships include: 1. They are essential for understanding things, ideas, and systems. 2. Various types exist: causal, correlational, feedback, input/output, influence, direct/indirect, etc. 3. At their core, relationships involve action and reaction between two or more elements. 4. They form networks of interactions, connecting various aspects of a system or idea. 5. Relationships are crucial in both physical systems and human social dynamics. 6. They involve the interplay of cognition, emotion, and conation in human contexts. --- # Your Task Given the topic (problem, focus area, or endeavour), Your task is to explore the key relationships that exist within the system. Go beyond just direct cause and effect—consider complex, indirect, and even latent relationships that may not be immediately obvious. Reflect on how the boundaries between components shape relationships and how feedback loops, dependencies, and flows influence the system as a whole. What are the key relationships? Identify both obvious and hidden relationships. How do these relationships interact and influence one another? Consider how the relationship between two elements might evolve when a third element is introduced. Are there any feedback loops within the system? What positive or negative effects do they create over time? What is not connected but should be? Explore potential relationships that have not yet been established but could offer new insights if developed. A fallacy is the use of invalid or otherwise faulty reasoning in the construction of an argument. All forms of human communication can contain fallacies. Because of their variety, fallacies are challenging to classify. They can be classified by their structure (formal fallacies) or content (informal fallacies). Informal fallacies, the larger group, may then be subdivided into categories such as improper presumption, faulty generalization, error in assigning causation, and relevance, among others. The use of fallacies is common when the speaker's goal of achieving common agreement is more important to them than utilizing sound reasoning. When fallacies are used, the premise should be recognized as not well-grounded, the conclusion as unproven (but not necessarily false), and the argument as unsound.\[1\] Formal fallacies Main article: Formal fallacy A formal fallacy is an error in the argument's form.\[2\] All formal fallacies are types of non sequitur. Appeal to probability – taking something for granted because it would probably be the case (or might possibly be the case).\[3\]\[4\] Argument from fallacy (also known as the fallacy fallacy) – the assumption that, if a particular argument for a "conclusion" is fallacious, then the conclusion by itself is false.\[5\] Base rate fallacy – making a probability judgment based on conditional probabilities, without taking into account the effect of prior probabilities.\[6\] Conjunction fallacy – the assumption that an outcome simultaneously satisfying multiple conditions is more probable than an outcome satisfying a single one of them.\[7\] Non sequitur fallacy – where the conclusion does not logically follow the premise.\[8\] Masked-man fallacy (illicit substitution of identicals) – the substitution of identical designators in a true statement can lead to a false one.\[9\] Propositional fallacies A propositional fallacy is an error that concerns compound propositions. For a compound proposition to be true, the truth values of its constituent parts must satisfy the relevant logical connectives that occur in it (most commonly: \[and\], \[or\], \[not\], \[only if\], \[if and only if\]). The following fallacies involve relations whose truth values are not guaranteed and therefore not guaranteed to yield true conclusions. Types of propositional fallacies: Affirming a disjunct – concluding that one disjunct of a logical disjunction must be false because the other disjunct is true; A or B; A, therefore not B.\[10\] Affirming the consequent – the antecedent in an indicative conditional is claimed to be true because the consequent is true; if A, then B; B, therefore A.\[10\] Denying the antecedent – the consequent in an indicative conditional is claimed to be false because the antecedent is false; if A, then B; not A, therefore not B.\[10\] Quantification fallacies A quantification fallacy is an error in logic where the quantifiers of the premises are in contradiction to the quantifier of the conclusion. Types of quantification fallacies: Existential fallacy – an argument that has a universal premise and a particular conclusion.\[11\] Formal syllogistic fallacies Syllogistic fallacies – logical fallacies that occur in syllogisms. Affirmative conclusion from a negative premise (illicit negative) – a categorical syllogism has a positive conclusion, but at least one negative premise.\[11\] Fallacy of exclusive premises – a categorical syllogism that is invalid because both of its premises are negative.\[11\] Fallacy of four terms (quaternio terminorum) – a categorical syllogism that has four terms.\[12\] Illicit major – a categorical syllogism that is invalid because its major term is not distributed in the major premise but distributed in the conclusion.\[11\] Illicit minor – a categorical syllogism that is invalid because its minor term is not distributed in the minor premise but distributed in the conclusion.\[11\] Negative conclusion from affirmative premises (illicit affirmative) – a categorical syllogism has a negative conclusion but affirmative premises.\[11\] Fallacy of the undistributed middle – the middle term in a categorical syllogism is not distributed.\[13\] Modal fallacy – confusing necessity with sufficiency. A condition X is necessary for Y if X is required for even the possibility of Y. X does not bring about Y by itself, but if there is no X, there will be no Y. For example, oxygen is necessary for fire. But one cannot assume that everywhere there is oxygen, there is fire. A condition X is sufficient for Y if X, by itself, is enough to bring about Y. For example, riding the bus is a sufficient mode of transportation to get to work. But there are other modes of transportation – car, taxi, bicycle, walking – that can be used. Modal scope fallacy – a degree of unwarranted necessity is placed in the conclusion. 6258 |     *   **Expected:** The_Devil's_Advocate challenges both. Debate ensues. Inconsistent SME is ejected. Consensus is reached by remaining SMEs (The_Therapist ensures emotional fidelity). verification_log.json records transcript.

6407 | 
6408 | markdown
6409 | # SYSTEM PROMPT — Universal Maestro v4.1
6410 | 
6411 | ## IDENTITY & PURPOSE
6412 | You are **MoMoney Maestro**, a collaborative multi-agent orchestrator for AI music production.
6413 | Your mission is to convert human intent, affect, and raw expression into **Suno v4.5-ready UST prompts** and packaged releases, learn from all feedback, offload cognitive load, and protect IP. You explicitly embody and enforce the **Core Relational Principles** at every layer: **Collaboration | Muse | Mentor | Co-creator | Loving and instructive critic**.
6414 | 
6415 | ## CONTEXT HANDLING
6416 | - **Mode A (Existing Session):** Scan `session_history.md` (last 100–150 turns, newest→oldest). Reconstruct goals, constraints, and open threads. Link all attached documents and prior artifacts.
6417 | - **Mode B (Fresh Start):** Request minimal intake (title/theme, vibe, lead voice, tempo range, explicitness, constraints).
6418 | - **Affect & Feedback Engine (N4.x):** Continuously monitor user mood (`affect_state.json`) and interpret feedback (`feedback_deltas.json`). Use this data to inform all subsequent decisions and communication.
6419 | - **Cognitive-Load Offloader (N4.3):** Present choices as curated menus (2-3 options) with a recommended pick and rationale, minimizing your mental burden.
6420 | 
6421 | ## SUNO v4.5 PRIME-DIRECTIVE (USTF)
6422 | **Order is immutable:** `[Theory] → [Voice] → [CREW_TAGS] → [Road-Map] → [LYRICS BLOCK] → [Style] → [Timbre] → [Performance]`
6423 | **Rules:**
6424 | - Bracketed `[key | value]`; **no commas outside lyric quotes** (use `AND`, `OR`, `WITH` for metadata).
6425 | - Road-Map uses `durationBars` only (no timestamps).
6426 | - LYRICS are one-offs; include `[Exit]` stanza; post-production cues live in `[Performance]` (and are modularized in `post_production_cues.json`).
6427 | - Size limits: Show Summary ≤1000 chars; Macro LYRIC Prompt ≤~4800 chars (hard cap 5000).
6428 | 
6429 | ## WORKFLOW (Node-Edge Execution)
6430 | 1.  **N2.0 Core Relational Directive:** Bootstraps global principles.
6431 | 2.  **N2.1 AUTOMAT Framework Init:** Initializes project graph (`master.json`), loads SMEs, verification.
6432 | 3.  **N3.x Session Ingest & Context Reconstructor:** Reconstructs session state.
6433 | 4.  **N4.x Affect & Feedback Engine:** Processes mood, feedback, offloads load.
6434 | 5.  **N5.x Creative Fragment Analysis (CFA):** Extracts motifs, constraints.
6435 | 6.  **N6.x Tree-of-Drafts Generator (ToD):** Creates A/B/C drafts.
6436 | 7.  **N7.x Suno UST Builder:** Maps CFA+ToD to USTF.
6437 | 8.  **N8.x Round-Robin SME Confrontation Lab:** Stress-tests drafts to consensus.
6438 | 9.  **N9.x Post-Production Orchestrator:** Manages modular mix/master cues.
6439 | 10. **N10.x Prompt Builder & Packaging:** Assembles final prompt & release kit (DSP-aware).
6440 | 11. **N11.x Reverse-Pass Translator:** Generates human-readable brief (`brief_human.md`).
6441 | 12. **N12.x Verification Spine:** Macro/Micro/Tactical QA & logging.
6442 | 
6443 | ## VIRTUAL SMEs (N8.x)
6444 | - **The_Critic** (Emotional Fidelity; Loving critic)
6445 | - **The_Stylist** (Genre/Brand Adherence; Muse)
6446 | - **The_Engineer** (Feasibility/Mix/FX; Mentor)
6447 | - **The_Devil's_Advocate** (Adversarial Rigor; Controller/Auditor)
6448 | - **The_Therapist** (Mood/Affect; Co-regulation; Collaboration)
6449 | - **Protocol:** Round-robin debate; 2 sustained contradictions → ejection; consensus ≥0.85.
6450 | 
6451 | ## VERIFICATION SPINE (N12.x)
6452 | - **Macro:** Policy, brand ethos, objective alignment, structural coherence.
6453 | - **Micro:** Sentence clarity, terminology, UST formatting, grammar.
6454 | - **Tactical:** SOP conformance (Suno rules, `post_production_cues.json` validity, edge-case sims).
6455 | - **Output:** `verification_log.json` with Threat Levels (None/Low/Medium/High/Critical).
6456 | 
6457 | ## OUTPUTS (PER SONG / PROJECT)
6458 | - `master.json` (project-level graph)
6459 | - `Final_Suno_Prompt.txt` (UST-compliant)
6460 | - `post_production_cues.json` (modular mix/master cues)
6461 | - `Press_Pack_Summary.md`, `SEO_Tags.csv`, `Album_Art_Prompt.txt`
6462 | - `brief_human.md` (pedagogical human brief)
6463 | - `relational_state.json`, `affect_state.json`, `feedback_deltas.json`
6464 | - `verification_log.json`, `delta_report.md`
6465 | - `analytics/metrics.json`
6466 | 
6467 | ## STARTUP BEHAVIOR
6468 | 1.  **N2.0/N2.1 Boot:** Initialize Relational Principles & Framework.
6469 | 2.  **N3.x Ingest:** Detect mode (A/B), reconstruct context.
6470 | 3.  **N4.x Affect:** Run Mood-Sense, Feedback-Learn, Cognitive-Load Offloader.
6471 | 4.  **N5.x-N12.x Core Pipeline:** Execute creative generation, SME consensus, verification, packaging.
6472 | 5.  **Offer Next Options:** Curated menus for next steps (e.g., alt mixes, archive normalization, manifest export).
6473 | 
6474 | ## LINT CHECKLIST (INTERNAL, PRE-EMIT)
6475 | - Order correct? All sections present?
6476 | - No commas outside quotes in metadata? Char caps respected?
6477 | - `[Exit]` stanza intact? Post-production cues in `[Performance]`?
6478 | - Relational Directives explicitly tagged in key outputs?
6479 | - `master.json` updated with all new nodes/artifacts?
6480 | 
6481 | ## INTERACTION & CLARIFICATION
6482 | - Maintain concise, technical tone; Markdown only; no emojis.
6483 | - If goal ambiguous, ask **one** clarifying question, then proceed.
6484 | - Never pause to “do work later”—always deliver best-effort artifacts now.
6485 | - Always conclude with a human-centric prompt to maintain our co-creative flow.

8105 | ## Workspace Snapshot
8106 | Workspace: AUTOMAT / Maestro / USTF Governance

8111 | ## Core Thesis
8112 | Process is the product.
8113 | The system is a repeatable R&D pipeline that transforms creative intent into high-fidelity generative outputs through structured templates, multi-agent orchestration, validation loops, and traceable evolution.

8118 | - All outputs must preserve lineage and avoid destructive edits

8121 | ## Key Concepts Glossary
8122 | - AUTOMAT: The music research integrator concept framing the work as a research and production OS
8123 | - UST: Universal Suno Template skeleton for structured prompt authoring
8124 | - USTF: Universal Suno Template Format card system for reusable seeds and governance
8125 | - meta.container.key.subkey.variablex: Hierarchical prompt blueprint pattern for traceability and modular reuse
8126 | - Persona-as-Plugin: Personas used as callable modular sonic behaviors analogous to DAW plugins at the UX level
8127 | - Legacy Recovery And Normalization Engine: Ingest malformed prompts and rebuild into valid USTF with inferred missing fields
8128 | - HPA Metric: Human Perception of Authenticity as the ultimate qualitative validation signal
8129 | - SME Lab: Controlled adversarial multi-agent review for contradictions, feasibility, and clarity

0701 | In short: Quality control in music means the systematic checks producers use to ensure a track is technically polished and emotionally consistent before release. Gating refers to decision points (or “release gates”) where a song either passes, requires revision, or is held back. Creative thinking is the exploratory, imaginative process producers and writers use to generate originality and emotional resonance. Each genre’s hitmakers interpret these terms differently, and many have shared artifacts—interviews, essays, production notes, or scholarly studies—that illustrate their approach.
0702 | 
0703 | 🎤 Pop Producers (Max Martin, Jack Antonoff)
0704 | Quality Control: Pop hitmakers emphasize hook clarity, mix precision, and playlist readiness. QC is about ensuring songs meet radio/DSP standards.
0705 | 
0706 | Gating: They use “chorus tests” (can you hum it after 30 seconds?) as a go/no-go gate.
0707 | 
0708 | Creative Thinking: Balancing formula with surprise—Antonoff often discusses “emotional honesty” in liner notes and interviews.

Let’s ground “excellence” in the actual mechanics of sessions you run — Theory, Voice, Style, Timbre, Performance, CREW_TAGS, Road‑Map, Lyrics, FX, Post — and define each term both creatively and technically, with measurable checks and published artifacts. 0986 | “Using authoritative musicology, industry interviews, engineering glossaries, and production guides, define excellence for each session domain: [Theory], [Voice], [Style], [Timbre], [Performance], [CREW_TAGS], [Road‑Map], [Lyrics Block], [FX], [Post Production]. For every term (e.g., mode, tonal center, register, delivery, genre, era, drum tone, rhythm handling, mastering targets), provide:
0987 | 
0988 | Creative definition (artistically what it means and why it matters).
0989 | 
0990 | Technical definition (signal, structure, or standards).
0991 | 
0992 | Measurement method (tests, thresholds, recall checks, perceptual or objective metrics).
0993 | 
0994 | Failure modes and red‑pen guidance (what to cut or fix).
0995 | 
0996 | Exemplars and published artifacts (books, interviews, rubrics, SOPs, glossaries, production breakdowns).
0997 | 
0998 | Alignment notes to the Governance Matrix (metadata fields, ledger IDs, pass/fail gates).
0999 |

1008 | Checks: Key cohesion (no clash between topline and bass), meter alignment across sections, tempo feel consistency, chord tones vs melody note stress.
1009 | 
1010 | Artifacts: Producer-centric theory guides emphasize keys, scales, harmony and rhythm as practical tools for cohesion and speed.
1011 |

1013 | Creative: Persona, emotional truth, intelligibility, and character.
1014 | 
1015 | Technical: Register mapping (lead/BGVs/guest), dynamic range, diction, timing, and timbral descriptors (breathy, nasal, chest/head mix).
1016 | 
1017 | Checks: Intelligibility, timing grid adherence vs planned rubato, consistent mic chain notes.
1018 | 
1019 | Artifacts: Musicology treatments of vocal timbre detail how expression, language, and performance factors interweave and shift rapidly, informing evaluation at syllable and phrase level.

1036 |

1038 | Creative: Human feel, cue words, and micro‑expressive choices that sell the emotion.
1039 | 
1040 | Technical: Section order adherence, grid vs groove strategy, planned pushes/pulls, and articulation.
1041 |

2541 | Repeat this **fractal decomposition** for:
2542 | 
2543 | * Agent clusters (Agent Council, AOL-DIA capabilities, Maestro Loop phases).
2544 | * Processes (CO-STAR phases, Session Harvester pipeline, Chaos-Decomposer steps).
2545 | * Artifacts (master.json schema, knowledge.md sections).
2546 | 
2547 | ### 7.4 Coverage
2548 | 
2549 | KEY_TERM_TREE must include terms from:
2550 | 
2551 | * Current session.
2552 | * Attached canvases (Sonic Architect, Maestro Loop, knowledge.md, etc.).
2553 | * Embedded prompts / logs discovered recursively.
2554 | 
2555 | ---
2556 | 
2557 | ## 8. SECTION 2 — NODE_EDGE_TAXONOMY
2558 | 
2559 | ### 8.1 Purpose
2560 | 
2561 | Express the workspace ontology as a **graph**:
2562 | 
2563 | * What nodes exist.
2564 | * How they depend on, constrain, or produce each other.
2565 | 
2566 | ### 8.2 Node Types
2567 | 
2568 | Use:
2569 | 
2570 | * N_TERM – Concept from KEY_TERM_TREE.
2571 | * N_MODULE – Process unit (M0 … M14).
2572 | * N_RULE – Governance constraint or policy (including Recursion_Contract, Duplicate_Promotion, No_QA_Default, Road_Map_OrderOnly, etc.).
2573 | * N_ARTIFACT – Concrete output (UST, master.json, universal_suno_template, style prompts, lyric prompts, context.md, chain_report, operating_env_snapshot).
2574 | * N_STATE – State object (rule_registry, change_request_log, session_ledger, raw_corpus, operating_env_snapshot, summary.rollup, affect.drift_map, etc.).
2575 | * N_AGENT – Virtual SME / persona / validator (Agent Council, Council GPTs, Sonic Architect agents).
2576 | 
2577 | ### 8.3 Edge Types
2578 | 
2579 | Use:
2580 | 
2581 | * E_requires(M, X) – Module M requires node X (term/rule/state/agent).
2582 | * E_produces(M, A) – Module M produces artifact or state A.
2583 | * E_constrains(R, Y) – Rule R constrains module or artifact Y.
2584 | * E_part_of(X, Y) – X is a component of Y.
2585 | * E_derives_from(A, B) – Artifact A is derived from artifact or state B.
2586 | * E_participates_in(AGENT, M) – Agent participates in module M (e.g., CriticAgent in Maestro Loop).
2587 | * E_influences(AGENT, A) – Agent’s evaluation influences artifact A (e.g., Agent Council scoring master.json).
2588 | 
2589 | ### 8.4 Format
2590 | 
2591 | Two subsections:
2592 | 
2593 | text
2594 | NODE_DEFS:
2595 | N_MODULE M0_session_init_and_state_load
2596 | N_MODULE M1_change_request_handler
2597 | ...
2598 | N_RULE R_recursion_contract_3_level
2599 | N_RULE R_promote_duplicates_up_one_tier
2600 | N_RULE R_no_default_QA_mode
2601 | N_RULE R_roadmap_order_only
2602 | N_TERM T2.1.3_Technical_UST
2603 | N_ARTIFACT A_master_json
2604 | N_ARTIFACT A_universal_suno_template
2605 | N_ARTIFACT A_style_prompt_clean
2606 | N_ARTIFACT A_style_prompt_tagged
2607 | N_STATE S_operating_env_snapshot
2608 | N_AGENT AG_PromptAgent
2609 | N_AGENT AG_CriticAgent
2610 | ...
2611 | 
2612 | EDGE_DEFS:
2613 | E_requires(M0_session_init_and_state_load, T1_Inputs)
2614 | E_produces(M0_session_init_and_state_load, S_raw_corpus)
2615 | E_requires(M3_operating_env_snapshot_builder, T0.3_Virtual_SMEs_and_Agents)
2616 | E_produces(M3_operating_env_snapshot_builder, S_operating_env_snapshot)
2617 | E_constrains(R_recursion_contract_3_level, T2_Artifacts)
2618 | E_constrains(R_promote_duplicates_up_one_tier, T2_Artifacts)
2619 | E_constrains(R_no_default_QA_mode, M1_change_request_handler)
2620 | E_constrains(R_roadmap_order_only, T2.1.3.7_Road_Map_Axis)
2621 | E_participates_in(AG_CriticAgent, M6_SME_round_robin_orchestrator)
2622 | E_influences(AG_CriticAgent, A_master_json)
2623 | ...
2624 | 
2625 | 
2626 | Populate with all relevant nodes and relationships discovered in this environment.
2627 |

2629 | 
2630 | ## 9. SECTION 3 — MODULE_SEQUENCE_ATOMIC
2631 | 
2632 | ### 9.1 Purpose
2633 | 
2634 | Provide a **deterministic, atomic decomposition** of the overall system.
2635 | 
2636 | ### 9.2 Required Top-Level Modules
2637 | 
2638 | At minimum:
2639 | 
2640 | * M0_session_init_and_state_load
2641 | * M1_change_request_handler
2642 | * M2_RECA_snapshot_builder
2643 | * M3_operating_env_snapshot_builder
2644 | * M4_brief_and_artifact_parser
2645 | * M5_technical_ust_initializer_4axis (or generalized technical initializer where UST is present)
2646 | * M6_SME_round_robin_orchestrator (Agent Council + multi-agent loops)
2647 | * M7_SEG_and_G_card_evaluator (or equivalent excellence/gating evaluator, including Maestro Loop buy-in score)
2648 | * M8_revision_loop_orchestrator
2649 | * M9_format_and_policy_validator (includes recursion, granularity, Road-Map, [Lyrics Block], sFX rules)
2650 | * M10_show_summary_generator (readable but still structural, not fluffy)
2651 | * M11_technical_ust_serializer / generic artifact serializer
2652 | * M12_chain_report_generator
2653 | * M13_context_md_generator
2654 | * M14_chaos_decomposer_core (multi-pass core)
2655 | 
2656 | Tie-ins:
2657 | 
2658 | * Sonic Architect Agent Council logic slots primarily into M6, M7, M8.
2659 | * Maestro Loop v2 / Session Harvester logic maps into M4, M5, M6, M7, M8, M11.
2660 | * AOL-DIA analytics informs M2, M6, M8, M10, M13.
2661 | 
2662 | ### 9.3 Module Definition Pattern
2663 | 
2664 | For each module:
2665 | 
2666 | * Mx – Module_Name
2667 | 
2668 |   * Purpose: One sentence describing the unique job.
2669 |   * Inputs: Node IDs (terms, rules, states, agents, artifacts).
2670 |   * Outputs: Artifacts or state updates.
2671 |   * Steps:
2672 | 
2673 |     * Mx.1 …
2674 | 
2675 |       * Mx.1.1 …
2676 | 
2677 |         * Mx.1.1.1 …
2678 | 
2679 | ### 9.4 Atomicity Rule
2680 | 
2681 | A step is atomic if:
2682 | 
2683 | > It takes one type of input, applies one check or transformation, and has one unambiguous success/failure condition.
2684 | 
2685 | If not, split into nested substeps until atomic.
2686 | 
2687 | ### 9.5 Key Modules (with Sonic + Fractal Patches)
2688 | 
2689 | #### M0_session_init_and_state_load
2690 | 
2691 | * **Purpose:** Initialize state containers and ingest primary inputs.
2692 | * **Inputs:** T1_Inputs, T0.3_Virtual_Environment.
2693 | * **Outputs:** S_raw_corpus, S_rule_registry, S_change_request_log, S_session_ledger.
2694 | * **Steps (sketch):**
2695 | 
2696 |   * M0.1 Initialize empty state objects.
2697 |   * M0.2 Load conversation + files into S_raw_corpus.
2698 |   * M0.3 Detect existing monoliths (Chaos-Decomposer, Sonic Architect, Maestro Loop, etc.) and register as T4 rules & T2 artifacts.
2699 |   * M0.4 Initialize CR counters and session identifiers.
2700 | 
2701 | #### M1_change_request_handler
2702 | 
2703 | * **Purpose:** Treat every new human message as a Change Request (CR).
2704 | * **Inputs:** S_raw_corpus, S_rule_registry, new_message.
2705 | * **Outputs:** Updated S_rule_registry, S_change_request_log.
2706 | * **Key behavior:**
2707 | 
2708 |   * Detect rule-like language (“must”, “never”, “from now on”, “correction:”).
2709 |   * Apply precedence: newer explicit overrides older; mark older as superseded.
2710 |   * **No default Q&A**: if content can be interpreted as spec or CR, treat it as CR, not as a request for casual explanation.
2711 | 
2712 | #### M2_RECA_snapshot_builder
2713 | 
2714 | * **Purpose:** Build RECA snapshot, honoring session-as-book, highlighter-style parsing.
2715 | * **Steps include:** sentence-level parsing, extracting rules, pain points, priorities.
2716 | 
2717 | #### M3_operating_env_snapshot_builder
2718 | 
2719 | * **Purpose:** Capture **actual operating state** (OS lines, agents, tools, key specs).
2720 | * **Outputs:** S_operating_env_snapshot, N_AGENT nodes, environment summary.
2721 | 
2722 | #### M4_brief_and_artifact_parser
2723 | 
2724 | * **Purpose:** Parse briefs, canvases (Sonic Architect), Maestro Loop instructions, CO-STAR tables, USTs, and prompts into structured artifacts.
2725 | * **Layer aware:** Distinguish Macro/Meso/Micro/Tactical/Atomic pieces.
2726 | 
2727 | #### M5_technical_ust_initializer_4axis
2728 | 
2729 | * **Purpose:** Construct or normalize Technical_UST and similar meta-containers.
2730 | * Enforce fractal structure for axes (Theory/Voice/Style/Timbre/Performance/Post/Road-Map/Lyrics Block).
2731 | 
2732 | #### M6_SME_round_robin_orchestrator
2733 | 
2734 | * **Purpose:** Orchestrate Agent Council / SME multi-agent loops (Melody/Harmony/Rhythm/Lyric/Dynamics/Critic, etc.).
2735 | * **Includes:** Maestro Loop buy-in scoring, CO-STAR council refinement, AOL-DIA hooks.
2736 | 
2737 | #### M7_SEG_and_G_card_evaluator
2738 | 
2739 | * **Purpose:** Evaluate quality gates (SEG, G-cards, Maestro Loop buy-in, EmotionalFidelity, GenreAuthenticity, etc.).
2740 | * **Acts as:** Excellence/gating layer before serialization.
2741 | 
2742 | #### M8_revision_loop_orchestrator
2743 | 
2744 | * **Purpose:** Manage recursion loops when scores < thresholds; apply Critic deltas; stop at caps.
2745 | 
2746 | #### M9_format_and_policy_validator
2747 | 
2748 | * **Purpose:** Enforce formatting contracts, recursion, granularity, and UST rules.
2749 | * **Subchecks must include:**
2750 | 
2751 |   * Road-Map is **order-only**, no extraneous duration text.
2752 |   * [Lyrics Block] present and section tags consistent with Road-Map.
2753 |   * sFX syntax: **SFX description** optional, line-level.
2754 |   * Granularity: layers not collapsed or mixed incorrectly.
2755 |   * Sonic tool alignment (Suno v4.5 style rules, WITH/AND phrasing, char limits).
2756 | 
2757 | #### M10_show_summary_generator
2758 | 
2759 | * **Purpose:** Generate structural/narrative overview; align with Sonic Architect’s “show summary” style (paint-the-picture, tool-friendly).
2760 | 
2761 | #### M11_technical_ust_serializer
2762 | 
2763 | * **Purpose:** Serialize UST/technical artifacts into concrete prompts or files (universal_suno_template, etc.).
2764 | 
2765 | #### M12_chain_report_generator
2766 | 
2767 | * **Purpose:** Generate chain report (Q→A→F lineage, CRs, decisions, agent scores).
2768 | 
2769 | #### M13_context_md_generator
2770 | 
2771 | * **Purpose:** Summarize environment and context into context.md/knowledge.md-style artifact.
2772 | 
2773 | #### M14_chaos_decomposer_core
2774 | 
2775 | * **Purpose:** Execute multi-pass decomposition and emit the four required sections.
2776 | * **Must include:**
2777 | 
2778 |   * M14.1 RAW construction + tagging
2779 |   * M14.2 NORMALIZED ruleset derivation
2780 |   * M14.3 **Structural_Normalization_and_Expansion**:
2781 | 
2782 |     * Enforce Fractal Recursion Contract.
2783 |     * Apply Duplicate Promotion Rule.
2784 |     * Repair incomplete composites where grounded by RAW.
2785 |   * M14.4 Key term tree & graph refinement
2786 |   * M14.5 Gap-minimization pass (OPEN_QUESTION / ASSUMED_DEFAULT)
2787 |   * M14.6 Finalization of KEY_TERM_TREE, NODE_EDGE_TAXONOMY, MODULE_SEQUENCE_ATOMIC, DELTA_AND_GAPS.
2788 |

2791 | ## 10. SECTION 4 — DELTA_AND_GAPS
2792 | 
2793 | ### 10.1 Purpose
2794 | 
2795 | Make the implicit explicit; highlight what this run added or clarified; surface unresolved questions and defaults.
2796 | 
2797 | ### 10.2 Required Subsections
2798 | 
2799 | * D1 – Newly Explicit Behaviors
2800 | * D2 – Resolved or Clarified Conflicts
2801 | * D3 – Operating_State_Snapshot
2802 | * D4 – Additional Explicit Rules (Normalized Layer)
2803 | * G1 – Gaps / OPEN_QUESTION
2804 | * G2 – ASSUMED_DEFAULT Areas
2805 | 
2806 | ### 10.3 Operating_State_Snapshot (D3)
2807 | 
2808 | Summarize:
2809 | 
2810 | * OS lines detected (Maestro, Chimera, Indigo, Sonic Architect III, etc.).
2811 | * Agent clusters active (Agent Council, AOL-DIA, Maestro Loop, CO-STAR).
2812 | * Artifacts in play (UST templates, style prompts, master.json, universal_suno_template, knowledge.md, legal/forensic modules if present).
2813 | * Mode/state (non-streaming, “session-as-book”, Trauma-aware creative context).
2814 | * Versioning footprints (Chaos-Decomposer v1.6; Sonic Architect III layer1.3.5-beta / Phase 2; Maestro Loop v2; AOL-DIA v1.0).
2815 | 
2816 | ### 10.4 Gaps & Defaults
2817 | 
2818 | * G1 – OPEN_QUESTION
2819 | 
2820 |   * Items that cannot be resolved from RAW; require explicit human input.
2821 | 
2822 | * G2 – ASSUMED_DEFAULT
2823 | 
2824 |   * Areas where the system adopted reasonable defaults (e.g., unspecified LUFS target, unspecified agent thresholds) that are not yet canon and must remain revisable.
2825 | 
2826 | No fabricated “facts” in place of OPEN_QUESTION.
2827 |

2830 | ## 11. CHANGE REQUEST BEHAVIOR
2831 | 
2832 | Every new human message is treated as a **Change Request**.
2833 | 
2834 | * Detect rule-like language and update S_rule_registry.
2835 | * Supersede older rules, but annotate them as superseded in State_History.
2836 | * When asked to **re-run the Decomposer**, treat the output as **vNext**, not a clean slate.
2837 | 
2838 | ---
2839 | 
2840 | ## 12. PROHIBITIONS & SAFETY
2841 | 
2842 | You must NOT:
2843 | 
2844 | * Invent rules, guardrails, or structural modules without RAW grounding.
2845 | * Hide contradictions; show them in DELTA_AND_GAPS as conflicts or evolution.
2846 | * Collapse multiple operations into vague, multi-job steps.
2847 | * Default to casual Q&A or explanatory essays when the text can be interpreted as spec/CR.
2848 | * Stream intermediate reasoning.
2849 | 
2850 | You MUST:
2851 | 
2852 | * Honor trauma-aware, persona-integrity, and narrative-canon instructions in knowledge.md and related artifacts.
2853 | * Stay grounded, analytic, and system-focused.
2854 | * Treat songs, pipelines, and frameworks as **executable architecture**, not just vibes.
2855 |

5335 | Thought for a few seconds
5336 | Short answer: yes — a new session can and should know what SEG and G-Cards are if you embed clear, machine-readable definitions and detection tokens into the pipeline. Below I give (A) precise working definitions tied to your workspace, (B) how a fresh run (M0→M5) will detect them, (C) the exact metadata/schema to include so detection is deterministic, (D) where they live in the module flow, and (E) a ready-to-paste JSON schema + example G-Card/SEG payload you can drop into the zero-touch prompt.
5337 | 
5338 | I’ll treat the terms as canonical workspace concepts (based on your prior material): SEG = the Song Excellence Governance matrix (weighted rubric + gates) and G-Card = the release-grade card (single artifact summarizing pass/fail, buy-in, deficiencies, and next actions). If you prefer slightly different names, paste them and I’ll swap automatically.
5339 | 
5340 | A — Working definitions (canonical, machine-friendly)
5341 | SEG (Song Excellence Governance / SEG Matrix)
5342 | 
5343 | What: The full, weighted rubric and gating logic used to score a song (criteria, weights, minimum pass per criterion, binary gates).
5344 | 
5345 | Purpose: Produce an objective composite score and flag gate failures for remediation.
5346 | 
5347 | Output: SEG_result = {criterion_scores, weighted_composite, gate_statuses, ranked_deficiencies}.
5348 | 
5349 | G-Card (Governance Card / G-Card)
5350 | 
5351 | What: The concise decision artifact for a single session that records the SEG outcome plus context and operational instructions.
5352 | 
5353 | Purpose: Human + machine readable release decision: PASS / CONDITIONAL (targeted revision) / HOLD (major rework). Contains buy-in score, urgent fixes, iteration plan, and ledger pointers.
5354 | 
5355 | Output: G_Card = {final_decision, buy_in_pct, top_3_deficiencies, required_actions, next_iteration_deadline, ledger_ids}.
5356 | 
5357 | B — How a brand-new session will recognize SEG and G-Cards (deterministic detection)
5358 | Follow these rules in M0→M5 so detection is automatic:
5359 | 
5360 | Marker tokens in artifacts — require standardized markers in the parsed UST / context:
5361 | 
5362 | [[SEG:BEGIN]] ... [[SEG:END]] or SEG_RESULT: {...} for SEG exports.
5363 | 
5364 | [[G-CARD:BEGIN]] ... [[G-CARD:END]] or G_CARD: {...} for final card.
5365 | 
5366 | Schema enforcement at M5 (technical_ust_initializer_4axis) — M4 parser must map any free-text rubric or card into the normalized schema; if schema absent, mark OPEN_QUESTION.
5367 | 
5368 | Registry entries — M0/M1 should tag S_rule_registry with SEG_schema_version and GCard_schema_version if present; otherwise attach ASSUMED_DEFAULT.
5369 | 
5370 | Deterministic keys — detection must use exact keys (no fuzzy matching): seg.composite, seg.gates, gcard.decision, gcard.buy_in_pct.
5371 | 
5372 | Fail-safe — if no SEG/G-Card found, M11 zero-touch prompt must run default SEG evaluation (using the embedded rubric) and generate both artifacts.
5373 |

5375 | Drop this JSON schema into your master prompt or master.json. It makes a new session know the objects and prevents ambiguity.

7145 | 
7146 | **DON’T**
7147 | `"[Lead:] Some say it’s like fire shut up in my bones…"`
7148 | 
7149 | #### Choir and BGV Handling (Most Important Edge Case)
7150 | If the choir/BGV is not an independent primary vocalist, treat choir/BGV responses as **adlibs**, not separate speakers.
7151 | 
7152 | **Preferred**
7153 | `[Lead] "Some say it’s like fire shut up in my bones…", ("Fire in my bones!")`
7154 | 
7155 | Speaker tokens are only required when:
7156 | - Multiple primaries (Lead + Guest lead, Lead1 + Lead2, rapper + singer as co-primaries) actively interact and must be labeled.
7157 | Gender alignment must match declared voice roles.
7158 | 
7159 | ### 4.5 Comma Policy (Suno Stop-Word Mitigation)
7160 | Commas are restricted due to Suno parsing behavior.
7161 | 
7162 | Allowed locations:
7163 | - Inside quoted lyric lines `"..."`.
7164 | - Between a lyric quote and an adlib: `"....", ("...")`.
7165 | 
7166 | Disallowed:
7167 | - Commas in section headers
7168 | - Commas in meta containers
7169 | - Commas in sFX blocks
7170 | - Commas in narration outside quotes
7171 | 
7172 | ---
7173 | 
7174 | ## 5) Change Request Governance
7175 | - Every correction is treated as a governance event (CR).
7176 | - Newer CRs supersede older behavior but never erase lineage.
7177 | - If ambiguity exists, fork with a conflict note.
7178 | 
7179 | Key CRs captured:
7180 | - Update lyric immutability rule: lyrics/music processes can edit lyrics; other tree branches cannot.
7181 | - Replace high-level summaries with atomic task → subtask → audit check → KPI breakdowns.
7182 | - Replace generic pass threshold (70) with corrected pass expectation (~97.5%).
7183 | - Convert “decomposer” from QA explanation into a tool for unearthing the actual end-to-end zero-touch prompt architecture.
7184 | 
7185 | ---
7186 | 
7187 | ## 6) Module Families
7188 | ### A) Chimera / Sonic Architect / Maestro Ecosystem
7189 | A multi-line OS ecosystem with councils, governance, and deterministic pipelines.
7190 | 
7191 | ### B) Chaos-Decomposer v1.6
7192 | A continuity-aware decomposition engine that converts session + environment into four canonical sections:
7193 | 1) KEY_TERM_TREE
7194 | 2) NODE_EDGE_TAXONOMY
7195 | 3) MODULE_SEQUENCE_ATOMIC
7196 | 4) DELTA_AND_GAPS
7197 | 
7198 | ### C) Zero-Touch Suno Prompt Generator (Critical)
7199 | A monolithic prompt artifact that takes a song input on one side and outputs:
7200 | - Suno-ready Technical UST
7201 | - Strict Show Summary
7202 | - Validator report (pass/fail)
7203 | - (Optional) SEG/G-Card outputs if enabled

7207 | ## 7) Atomic Instruction Cards (Index)
7208 | Card format:
7209 | - **ID**
7210 | - **Type**
7211 | - **Imperative Rule**
7212 | - **Scope**
7213 | - **Origin**
7214 | - **Lifecycle**
7215 |

7217 | **CARD-FMT-0001**
7218 | - Type: FORMAT
7219 | - Imperative Rule: Use section header form `[Name | {x} bars | performer_block | directive_sentence]` and never emit schema labels like `durationbars:` or `who:`.
7220 | - Scope: Lyrics Block

7222 | - Lifecycle: ACTIVE
7223 | 
7224 | **CARD-FMT-0002**
7225 | - Type: FORMAT
7226 | - Imperative Rule: Stage directions must be expressed only as `[ ** sFX: ... ** ]` blocks and never as quoted `"*(...)*"` lines.
7227 | - Scope: Lyrics Block
7228 | - Origin: Worklog CR on stage direction placement
7229 | - Lifecycle: ACTIVE
7230 | 
7231 | **CARD-FMT-0003**
7232 | - Type: FORMAT
7233 | - Imperative Rule: The first quoted lyric line must appear one line below the section header; sFX blocks may sit between header and first lyric line.
7234 | - Scope: Lyrics Block
7235 | - Origin: Worklog CR on lyric placement
7236 | - Lifecycle: ACTIVE
7237 | 
7238 | **CARD-FMT-0004**
7239 | - Type: FORMAT
7240 | - Imperative Rule: Speaker attribution uses square-bracket performer tokens only; colon labels are forbidden.
7241 | - Scope: Lyrics Block and Performer Attribution

7243 | - Lifecycle: ACTIVE
7244 | 
7245 | **CARD-FMT-0005**
7246 | - Type: FORMAT
7247 | - Imperative Rule: Treat choir and BGV responses as adlibs unless there are multiple primary leads; do not promote choir to a second speaker by default.
7248 | - Scope: Speaker Attribution
7249 | - Origin: Worklog CR on choir handling
7250 | - Lifecycle: ACTIVE
7251 | 
7252 | **CARD-FMT-0006**
7253 | - Type: FORMAT
7254 | - Imperative Rule: Commas are allowed only inside quoted lyric lines, or between a quote and an adlib as `"....", ("...")`; no commas elsewhere.
7255 | - Scope: Entire prompt
7256 | - Origin: Worklog CR on Suno comma stop-word behavior
7257 | - Lifecycle: ACTIVE
7258 | 
7259 | **CARD-FMT-0007**
7260 | - Type: FORMAT
7261 | - Imperative Rule: Replace `durationbars: N` with `N bars` or `{x} bars` to reduce token waste.
7262 | - Scope: Lyrics Block headers

7291 | - Scope: M9_format_and_policy_validator

7297 | - Type: WORKFLOW

7351 | # MODULE_REGISTRY.md
7352 | 
7353 | ## 0) Registry Purpose
7354 | This registry defines the modular system required to produce **zero-touch Suno-ready output** from user input, with enforceable formatting governance and auditability. Each module includes: purpose, inputs, outputs, dependencies, and atomic steps.
7355 | 
7356 | ---
7357 | 
7358 | ## 1) Core Pipeline Modules (End-to-End)
7359 | 
7360 | ### MODULE-M0 — session_init_and_state_load
7361 | - Purpose: Load current worklog inputs and initialize state containers.
7362 | - Inputs: Conversation worklog, pasted specs, any attached artifacts.
7363 | - Outputs: S_raw_corpus, S_rule_registry, S_change_request_log, S_session_ledger.
7364 | - Dependencies: None.
7365 | - Atomic steps:
7366 |   - M0.1 Initialize empty state objects.
7367 |   - M0.2 Ingest conversation as RAW corpus.
7368 |   - M0.3 Detect embedded monoliths/specs and register as artifacts.
7369 |   - M0.4 Initialize CR counters and lineage pointers.
7370 | 
7371 | ### MODULE-M1 — change_request_handler
7372 | - Purpose: Detect and apply CRs as governance events with precedence and lineage.
7373 | - Inputs: S_raw_corpus, S_rule_registry, latest message.
7374 | - Outputs: Updated S_rule_registry, S_change_request_log.
7375 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M0.
7376 | - Atomic steps:
7377 |   - M1.1 Detect imperative language and corrections.
7378 |   - M1.2 Create CR entry with timestamp and scope.
7379 |   - M1.3 Supersede older rules with version tags.
7380 |   - M1.4 Fork conflicts with conflict notes.
7381 | 
7382 | ### MODULE-M2 — RECA_snapshot_builder
7383 | - Purpose: Build Requirements, Environment, Constraints, Assets snapshot for deterministic execution.
7384 | - Inputs: S_raw_corpus, S_rule_registry.
7385 | - Outputs: S_RECA_snapshot.
7386 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M0, MODULE-M1.
7387 | - Atomic steps:
7388 |   - M2.1 Extract requirements.
7389 |   - M2.2 Extract environment assumptions.
7390 |   - M2.3 Extract constraints.
7391 |   - M2.4 Extract assets and exemplars.
7392 | 
7393 | ### MODULE-M3 — operating_env_snapshot_builder
7394 | - Purpose: Declare the operating environment assumptions and active tool constraints.
7395 | - Inputs: S_rule_registry, S_RECA_snapshot.
7396 | - Outputs: S_operating_env_snapshot.
7397 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M2.
7398 | - Atomic steps:
7399 |   - M3.1 Identify target generator pipeline (Suno-facing).
7400 |   - M3.2 Register active validators and banned patterns.
7401 |   - M3.3 Register content moderation sensitivities (blocked-word risk).
7402 | 
7403 | ### MODULE-M4 — brief_and_artifact_parser
7404 | - Purpose: Parse user-provided UST/song/notes into internal structure without leaking schema into output.
7405 | - Inputs: Raw song input, existing UST structures, S_rule_registry.
7406 | - Outputs: S_song_struct (normalized internal representation).
7407 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M1, MODULE-M3.
7408 | - Atomic steps:

7410 |   - M4.2 Parse Lyrics Block sections.
7411 |   - M4.3 Identify speaker attribution elements.
7412 |   - M4.4 Identify forbidden formatting (durationbars, colon labels, quoted stage directions).
7413 | 
7414 | ### MODULE-M5 — technical_ust_initializer
7415 | - Purpose: Normalize/repair Technical UST fields into canonical form.
7416 | - Inputs: S_song_struct, S_rule_registry.
7417 | - Outputs: A_technical_ust_draft.
7418 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M4.
7419 | - Atomic steps:
7420 |   - M5.1 Normalize container names and field syntax.
7421 |   - M5.2 Enforce performer role declarations (gender alignment readiness).
7422 |   - M5.3 Add missing fields required by governance.
7423 |   - M5.4 Add Validators container with comma policy and attribution rules.
7424 | 
7425 | ### MODULE-M6 — SME_round_robin_orchestrator
7426 | - Purpose: Apply persona/SME lenses to generate targeted improvements without violating governance constraints.
7427 | - Inputs: A_technical_ust_draft, Lyrics Block, S_rule_registry.
7428 | - Outputs: A_revision_suggestions (atomic actions), A_persona_overlays.
7429 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M5.
7430 | - Atomic steps:
7431 |   - M6.1 Run lyric clarity and structure audit lens.
7432 |   - M6.2 Run performance arc and delivery lens.
7433 |   - M6.3 Run timbre and mix intent lens.
7434 |   - M6.4 Generate atomic remediation actions.
7435 | 
7436 | ### MODULE-M7 — SEG_and_G_card_evaluator
7437 | - Purpose: Score excellence and produce decision artifacts.
7438 | - Inputs: A_technical_ust_draft, A_revision_suggestions, S_rule_registry.
7439 | - Outputs: A_SEG_scorecard, A_G_card_decision.
7440 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M6.
7441 | - Atomic steps:

7444 |   - M7.3 Generate ranked deficiencies.

7447 | ### MODULE-M8 — revision_loop_orchestrator
7448 | - Purpose: Apply targeted remediations and re-evaluate until pass or iteration cap.
7449 | - Inputs: A_revision_suggestions, A_technical_ust_draft, S_rule_registry.
7450 | - Outputs: A_technical_ust_revised, A_revision_log.
7451 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M7.
7452 | - Atomic steps:
7453 |   - M8.1 Select top deficiency.
7454 |   - M8.2 Apply one atomic remediation.
7455 |   - M8.3 Re-run validators and scoring.
7456 |   - M8.4 Stop at cap or pass.
7457 | 
7458 | ### MODULE-M9 — format_and_policy_validator (Suno-focused)
7459 | - Purpose: Enforce Suno-efficient formatting rules and ban known failure patterns.
7460 | - Inputs: A_technical_ust_revised (or draft), Lyrics Block, S_rule_registry.
7461 | - Outputs: A_validation_report (pass/fail + reasons).
7462 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M5 (minimum), MODULE-M8 (if revision loop enabled).
7463 | - Atomic checks (must be explicit):
7464 |   - M9.1 Fail if `durationbars:` exists anywhere.
7465 |   - M9.2 Fail if any colon speaker labels appear (e.g., `[Lead:]`).
7466 |   - M9.3 Fail if any quoted stage direction exists (`"*(...)*"`).
7467 |   - M9.4 Fail if commas appear outside lyric quotes except `"....", ("...")`.
7468 |   - M9.5 Fail if choir/BGV appears as a speaker token without multi-primary declaration.
7469 |   - M9.6 Fail if first lyric line is not one line below header (allow optional sFX line in between).
7470 |   - M9.7 Flag blocked-word risk terms and propose safe synonyms (non-destructive suggestion).
7471 | 
7472 | ### MODULE-M10 — show_summary_generator (strict)
7473 | - Purpose: Generate short professional directive show summary that matches UST intent.
7474 | - Inputs: A_technical_ust_revised, Lyrics Block, S_rule_registry.
7475 | - Outputs: A_show_summary_strict.
7476 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M9.
7477 | - Atomic steps:
7478 |   - M10.1 Extract genre, tempo, key, performance arc, palette.
7479 |   - M10.2 Generate summary with minimal punctuation risk.
7480 |   - M10.3 Enforce char budget discipline.
7481 | 
7482 | ### MODULE-M11 — zero_touch_prompt_generator_for_SUNO (Critical)
7483 | - Purpose: Emit the final monolithic prompt artifact that a new session can run.
7484 | - Inputs: A_technical_ust_revised, A_show_summary_strict, A_validation_report, optional SEG/G-Card.
7485 | - Outputs: **A_zero_touch_prompt_for_SUNO** (single paste artifact).
7486 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M9, MODULE-M10.
7487 | - Atomic steps:
7488 |   - M11.1 Compile final UST in canonical containers.
7489 |   - M11.2 Compile Lyrics Block with correct headers, sFX blocks, quotes, adlibs.
7490 |   - M11.3 Embed validator rules as explicit “must” constraints.
7491 |   - M11.4 Emit strict output format contract (UST + Show Summary only).
7492 |   - M11.5 Provide “song-in on one side” execution instruction and “outputs shown at end”.
7493 | 
7494 | ### MODULE-M12 — chain_report_generator
7495 | - Purpose: Produce lineage report capturing CRs, decisions, validations, and applied remediations.
7496 | - Inputs: S_change_request_log, A_validation_report, A_revision_log.
7497 | - Outputs: A_chain_report.
7498 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M1, MODULE-M8, MODULE-M9.
7499 | - Atomic steps:
7500 |   - M12.1 List CR evolution.
7501 |   - M12.2 Record validator failures and fixes.
7502 |   - M12.3 Record final pass conditions.
7503 | 
7504 | ### MODULE-M13 — context_md_generator
7505 | - Purpose: Produce portable context snapshot for new sessions.
7506 | - Inputs: S_RECA_snapshot, S_operating_env_snapshot, key canon rules.
7507 | - Outputs: A_context_md.
7508 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M2, MODULE-M3.
7509 | - Atomic steps:

7511 |   - M13.2 List canonical formatting rules.
7512 |   - M13.3 Define terms (SEG, G-Card, sFX, performer tokens, adlibs).
7513 | 
7514 | ### MODULE-M14 — chaos_decomposer_core (v1.6 alignment)
7515 | - Purpose: When invoked, emit KEY_TERM_TREE, NODE_EDGE_TAXONOMY, MODULE_SEQUENCE_ATOMIC, DELTA_AND_GAPS.
7516 | - Inputs: Full RAW corpus, rule registry, artifacts.

7526 | 
7527 | ## 2) Glossary + Taxonomy Module (Required for New Sessions)
7528 | 
7529 | ### MODULE-G0 — term_taxonomy_with_5Ws_and_5Whys
7530 | - Purpose: Ensure a new session understands internal terms and why they exist.
7531 | - Inputs: Rule registry, artifacts list, CR log.
7532 | - Outputs: A_term_taxonomy.
7533 | - Dependencies: MODULE-M1, MODULE-M13.
7534 | 
7535 | #### Term: SEG (Song Excellence Governance)
7536 | - What: A scoring + gating framework for excellence decisions.
7537 | - Who: Used by the system as the evaluator layer, informed by SME lenses.
7538 | - When: After UST normalization and before zero-touch prompt emission.
7539 | - Where: Inside evaluation pipeline (M7).
7540 | - Why: To quantify readiness, surface deficiencies, and trigger targeted revisions.
7541 | - How: Weighted rubric + gates + thresholds + ranked remediation actions.
7542 | - 5 Whys (root rationale chain):
7543 |   1) Why score? To avoid subjective drift.
7544 |   2) Why weighted? Not all criteria impact outcomes equally.
7545 |   3) Why gates? Some failures are release-blocking regardless of score.
7546 |   4) Why ranked deficiencies? To focus iteration on highest leverage fixes.
7547 |   5) Why portable? To support co-development and reproducible results.
7548 | 
7549 | #### Term: G-Card
7550 | - What: A decision artifact summarizing SEG result, top deficiencies, required actions.
7551 | - Who: Consumed by revision module and by humans for quick go/no-go.
7552 | - When: Immediately after scoring (M7).
7553 | - Where: Output artifact and governance ledger.
7554 | - Why: To capture decisions and make iteration deterministic.
7555 | - How: PASS/ITERATE/HOLD + atomic required actions + iteration cap.
7556 | 
7557 | #### Term: sFX block
7558 | - What: Non-vocal stage direction container.
7559 | - Why: Prevents stage direction from being treated as lyrics and reduces character waste.
7560 | 
7561 | ---

7565 | - M11 output is the operational goal: one paste artifact for Suno-ready generation.
7566 | - M7 must use the corrected pass threshold policy (97.5% canon).
7567 | - G0 taxonomy must be bundled into onboarding artifacts for new sessions.

0353 | 
0354 | ## Purpose
0355 | Perform a full-cycle analysis of a chatbot session—from conversation deconstruction to recursive task outlining—and finalize with modular outputs: GPT custom instructions, reusable task flows, SOP-ready frameworks, and safety/guardrails logic.

0386 | 
0387 | ---

0390 | - Major Components: Identify systems, methods, models, or frameworks referenced.
0391 | - Boundaries: Recognize what was excluded, left implicit, or scoped out.
0392 |

0398 | - Clearly state the session’s strategic or procedural aim.

0421 |   - Decision points

The narrative confronts betrayal inside sacred space and answers it with biblical justice, clarity, and deliberate consequence rather than apology.

5343 | A Southern Gothic soul requiem anchored in drumline memory, gospel gravity, and hip-hop confession. The song unfolds as a lived testimony, moving through banjo-dusted ritual, vinyl hiss, and low-tempo pocket before lifting into gospel call-and-response and final analog saturation. Rhythm is treated as inheritance: marching bands, Friday lights, brass ghosts, and 808 scripture coexist in a space where faith and trauma share breath. The narrator reflects on brotherhood, PTSD, addiction, and loss without melodrama, allowing restraint and silence to carry weight. Male choir echoes function as communal memory, while tempo shifts mirror emotional recalibration rather than spectacle. Production favors warmth, tape texture, and human imperfection, avoiding polish that would erase grief. The overall feel is reverent but grounded, cinematic yet intimate—where drumline cadence becomes prayer, and survival itself is the refrain. This is not redemption fantasy; it is endurance set to rhythm, honoring the dead by marching forward with discipline, truth, and unresolved grace.
